【The reality everyone forgets: the Swiss franc shock】

It is not a problem that can be dismissed with "if you choose your markets, don't make unreasonable trades, and keep enough margin to survive slippage, margin calls basically won't occur"

From FSA materials
A domestic FX broker, Company A, filled CHF/JPY at 117.698 yen at 18:34:33, then became unable to quote rates, and the next fill was 47 minutes 17 seconds later at 19:21:50, at 132.016 yen

At Company A, there was an actual case where it could not quote rates for a range of 14.318 yen in between

Even if you place a stop order at 118 or 120 yen, if there is no price at which it can be filled, it cannot be settled

A normal stop order is not a guarantee of stopping the loss at the specified price; after being triggered it becomes a market order and is filled at the next tradable price

This is not a story of slipping a few pips

It is a story of the price itself jumping, and a period during which neither stop-out nor stop orders could be executed

In fact, in Japan 1,229 cases of unrecovered debt occurred, totaling 3,388,000,000 yen

Overseas too, Alpari UK went bankrupt, and at FXCM customers' negative balances reached about $276 million and it received an emergency loan of $300 million

Of course, keeping a margin of safety and low leverage are important

But the real lesson is not

"I placed a stop order so I'm fine"

but

"trade a size that won't knock you out even if the stop order doesn't fill"

It is true that zero-cut in overseas FX is advantageous as a margin-call countermeasure

However, the flat assertion that "margin calls basically won't happen unless you make unreasonable trades" is refuted by the real example of the Swiss franc shock

2118663877881913558.content_en:
Explaining overseas FX payment collection agents with the mechanism of convenience-store payment...
(This is a typical payment collection agent)
This is the common flow when you shop online or pay an invoice.
•  Instead of transferring directly to the shop's bank account
•  You receive a "number (or barcode) you can pay at a convenience store"
•  You pay cash etc. at a Seven or FamilyMart
•  The convenience store (or the payment collection company behind it) receives the money for the time being
•  Later it sends the money in bulk to the real recipient (the shop)
Here the convenience store plays the role of "receiving money on your behalf and handing it to the recipient." This is payment collection. For you, the benefit is "it's easy because you can pay at a nearby shop."
In the case of overseas FX deposits
When you deposit to overseas FX by bank transfer, the structure is almost the same.
1.  You don't send directly to the overseas FX broker
2.  You transfer to the account of a domestic "payment collection agent" in Japan
3.  That agent receives the money for the time being
4.  And relays it to the overseas FX broker
In other words, the payment collection agent plays the role of the "convenience store" in convenience-store payment. It has been widely used because it is easier than remitting directly overseas and fees are easier to keep down.
Why is it called "gray"?
Convenience-store payment is made for legitimate domestic transactions in Japan, so it rarely becomes a problem.
For overseas FX, on the other hand:
•  The final recipient is an overseas firm unregistered in Japan
•  Money moves across borders (cross-border payment collection)
This act of "stepping in between and relaying" was traditionally considered a gray zone that was hard to fit into a clear regulatory framework. The 2026 revision of the Payment Services Act made this clearly subject to regulation, and the period during which it can continue without registration is now limited, which is the current situation.
In short, it is the same mechanism of "collecting money in between and handing it over," just as "the convenience store receives it in place of the invoice," but the point is that because it relays to an unregistered overseas firm, it is treated differently from ordinary convenience-store payment.
2118663877881913558.content_original:
海外FXの収納代行業者をコンビニ払いの仕組みで例えると…
（これが典型的な収納代行）
あなたがネット通販や請求書の支払いをする時よくある流れがこれです。
•  あなたが直接お店の銀行口座に振り込むのではなく
•  「コンビニで払える番号（またはバーコード）」をもらう
•  セブンやファミマで現金などを払う
•  コンビニ（またはその後ろにいる収納代行会社）がお金をいったん受け取る
•  後からまとめて本当の受取人（お店側）に送金する
このときコンビニは「お金を代わりに受け取って、受取人に渡す」役割をしています。これが収納代行です。あなたにとっては「近くの店で払えて楽」というメリットがあります。
海外FXの入金の場合
海外FXに銀行送金で入金するときも、構造はほぼ同じです。
1.  あなたは海外のFX業者に直接送金するのではなく
2.  日本国内の「収納代行業者」の口座に振り込む
3.  その業者がいったんお金を受け取り
4.  海外のFX業者に中継して送る
つまり、コンビニ払いの「コンビニ」の役割を、収納代行業者がやっている形です。直接海外に送金するより手軽で手数料も抑えやすいため、よく使われてきました。
なぜ「グレー」と言われるのか
コンビニ払いは、日本国内の正規の取引に対して行われるので問題になりにくいです。
一方、海外FXの場合は：
•  最終的な受け手が日本で無登録の海外業者
•  お金が国境をまたいで動く（クロスボーダー収納代行）
この「間に入って中継する」行為が、従来は明確な規制の枠組みに入りにくいグレーゾーンとされていました。2026年の資金決済法改正でこの点が明確に規制対象になり、登録なしで続けられる期間が限定的になっている、というのが現在の状況です。
要するに、「コンビニが請求書の代わりに受け取る」のと同じく「間に入ってお金を集めて渡す」仕組みなんですが、海外の無登録業者への中継という点で、普通のコンビニ払いとは扱いが違うという話です。

Now that overseas FX looks set to become harder to use because of the legal revision,
the voices saying "domestic FX is the only choice after all"
are conspicuous, as if on cue,

but what's important
isn't which one is better,

it's whether, even after it has become harder to use,
overseas FX still has a reason to keep using it.

That's the point, I think.

For example, in the case of EA users.

If you run multiple EAs in one account,
it's normal to hold many positions at the same time.

With domestic leverage of 25x
this is nowhere near enough,
and operation becomes quite cramped.

Overseas also has
・Higher leverage means you can deposit less
(the money saved can go into other investments)
・Bonuses that don't exist domestically
・Many brokers that offer MT5

There are definitely advantages that domestic doesn't have.

As for the argument that "domestic spreads are narrower,"
I think that's about brokers without MT5, isn't it?

MT5 is essential for EA users,
but there are only 4 domestic brokers that offer MT5 right now,

and while Gaitame Finest has quite narrow spreads,
the others are on par with narrow overseas brokers,
or often overseas is even cheaper.

Conversely, domestic has its own strengths:
favorable taxes and easy deposits and withdrawals.

Honestly, even I
would want to use domestic if leverage there became around 100x.

・Lay out all these factors
・And also factor in that bank deposits and withdrawals are likely to be regulated
and then judge whether it's still worth using

It's important to judge from that perspective.

Honestly, I think you don't need to listen much to opinions that completely deny one side.

【Sending by crypto = scary price swings is a misunderstanding】

When you hear crypto,
you probably picture something like Bitcoin
with violent price swings.

But what's used for overseas FX remittance
is not that,

it's something called a "stablecoin."

Roughly speaking, these are
cryptocurrencies built to keep the same value as the dollar or yen.

・USDC, USDT → 1 coin ≈ 1 dollar
・JPYC → 1 coin ≈ 1 yen

So you can basically assume that things like
"my funds dropped by 20% while I was sending them!"
don't happen.

With a dollar stablecoin,
from the yen side there's only the USD/JPY movement.
This is the same feel as ordinary foreign currency.

It relies on the issuer's credibility so the risk isn't completely zero,

but if you've been avoiding it thinking
"the price swings are too violent to use,"

it might be worth reconsidering ☺

というものです。

ドルや円と同じ値段を保つように作られた
仮想通貨のこと。

・USDC、USDT → 1枚≒1ドル

2119396458176684315.content_en:
During my recent stay in Japan, alongside the debate of "domestic FX, overseas FX, or prop," another big topic I noticed on X was the anime "FX Soldier Kurumi-chan". 📺

The "finger barrier" scene from the latest episode alone has been played over 1.4 million times in 2 days 👀

That's amazing.

Honestly, I think every trader has done it at least once. I have too 😅📊

On X right now there's a lively debate over whether it's "fun to watch or just painful," and I was torn at first too.

Is this work a plus or a minus for conveying FX and trading to a wide range of people in Japan?

It clearly depicts the negative side of trading, while the positive sides that I think there are plenty of are not necessarily all depicted.

Even so, overall I think it's "a good thing."

That attention is gathering on FX and trading, and that real risks and negative sides are depicted there. I think that is ultimately good for the industry. Even if not in the short term, definitely in the long term.

As a result, people about to start trading, and those who have already started, become more aware of the risks. That means fewer extreme failure stories, fewer people whose lives are ruined, and hopefully fewer margin calls and stop-outs. This is definitely a plus.

Trading is not easy, and it's not all good. I understand that well, and at Fintokei we try to convey exactly that.
That's why I'm excited about the very existence of this story and anime. I think it's quite unique. I was truly surprised when I first watched it. Because I can't imagine such a work being produced, broadcast and getting this much attention in the Czech Republic or Europe. It's a truly interesting phenomenon.

And if there were a way to introduce prop trading in the work as "another option," that is, as a means to help with discipline and risk management and keep distance from margin calls, that would be the best.

Hiding the chart with your fingers won't stop losses, but rules can. For people who fear risk, people not yet confident in their own trading, people not profitable over the long term, and people who struggle with their own discipline, risk management and following rules. Not for everyone, but especially for such people, I think prop trading is a very rational option.

Actually, I've already started looking for ways to work together with the production side. Of course nothing is decided and it may take time, but look forward to seeing what happens 👀

What did you think of this work?

And if "prop trading today" were introduced a little in the work, would you want to see it?
2119396458176684315.content_original:
先日の日本滞在中、「国内FXか、海外FXか、プロップか」という議論と並んで、Xでもうひとつ大きな話題になっていると気づいたのが、アニメ『FX戦士くるみちゃん』でした。📺

最新話の「指バリアー」のシーンだけで、2日で140万回以上も再生されています👀

すごいことです。

正直に言うと、トレーダーなら誰でも一度はやったことがあると思います。私もあります😅📊

今、Xでは「見ていて面白いのか、それとも苦しいだけなのか」という議論が盛り上がっていますが、私自身も最初は迷いました。

この作品は、FXやトレードを日本の幅広い層に伝えるうえで、プラスなのか、マイナスなのか。

トレードのネガティブな側面をはっきり描いている一方で、私がたくさんあると思っているポジティブな側面は、必ずしもすべて描かれているわけではないからです。

それでも、全体としては「良いこと」だと思っています。

FXやトレードに注目が集まり、そこに本当のリスクや負の側面が描かれていること。それは最終的に業界にとって良いことだと思います。短期的にはそうでなくても、長期的には間違いなく。

その結果として、これからトレードを始めようとしている方や、すでに始めている方が、リスクをより意識するようになる。それは、極端な失敗談が減り、人生を狂わせる人が減り、そして願わくは追証やロスカットも減るということです。これは間違いなくプラスです。

トレードは簡単ではないし、良いことばかりでもない。私はそれを十分に分かっていますし、Fintokeiでもまさにそのように伝えようとしています。
だから、この物語とアニメが存在すること自体に、私はワクワクしています。かなりユニークだと思います。初めて観たとき、本当に驚きました。チェコやヨーロッパで、こういう作品が制作され、放送され、これほど注目を集めることは想像できないからです。本当に興味深い現象です。

そして、もし作品の中でプロップトレードを「もうひとつの選択肢」として、つまり規律やリスク管理を助け、追証から距離を置くための手段として紹介できる方法があれば、最高だと思います。

指でチャートを隠しても損失は止まりませんが、ルールなら止められます。リスクが怖い方、自分のトレードにまだ自信がない方、長期的に利益を出せていない方、そして自分の規律やリスク管理、ルールを守ることに課題を感じている方。すべての方にとってではなく、特にそうした方にとって、プロップトレードはとても合理的な選択肢だと私は考えています。

実は、制作側の皆さんと何かご一緒できる方法がないか、すでに模索を始めています。もちろん何も決まっていませんし、時間のかかる話かもしれませんが、どうなるか楽しみにしていてください👀

皆さんは、この作品をどう感じましたか？

そして、作品の中で「今のプロップトレード」が少し紹介されたら、見てみたいと思いますか？
